summary: A husband may add as much as he wants to the kesubah. Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah says the extra is only paid if they got married, and Rabbi Meir says a kesubah may never be less than the set amount.

chunks.en: Even though the Sages said
chunks.st: Although they said as a principle

chunks.en: a maiden collects two hundred and a widow one hundred,
chunks.st: that a virgin collects two hundred dinars as payment for her marriage contract and that a widow collects one hundred dinars,

chunks.en: if he wants to add,
chunks.st: if the husband wishes to add

chunks.en: even ten thousand zuz,
chunks.st: even an additional ten thousand dinars,

chunks.en: he may add. If she became a widow or was divorced,
chunks.st: he may add it. If she is then widowed or divorced,

chunks.he: בֵּין מִן הָאֵרוּסִין בֵּין מִן הַנִּשּׂוּאִין,
chunks.en: whether after the erusin or after the marriage,
chunks.st: whether from betrothal or whether from marriage,

chunks.en: she collects all of it.
chunks.st: she collects the entire amount, including the additional sum.

chunks.en: Rabbi Elazar ben Azaryah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya says:

chunks.en: after the marriage,
chunks.st: If she is widowed or divorced from marriage,

chunks.en: she collects all of it.
chunks.st: she collects the total amount,

chunks.en: After the erusin,
chunks.st: but if she is widowed or divorced from betrothal,

chunks.en: a maiden collects two hundred and a widow one hundred,
chunks.st: a virgin collects two hundred dinars and a widow one hundred dinars.

chunks.en: because he wrote the extra for her only
chunks.st: This is because he wrote the additional amount for her in the marriage contract only

chunks.en: so that he could marry her.
chunks.st: in order to marry her.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says
chunks.stMore: a related halakha with regard to the marriage contract:

chunks.en: If he wants,
chunks.st: If he wishes,

chunks.en: he writes a document of two hundred for a maiden,
chunks.st: he may write for a virgin a document for two hundred dinars as is fitting for her,

chunks.en: and she writes,
chunks.st: and she may then write a receipt stating:

chunks.en: I got one hundred from you.
chunks.explain: She gives up half, without really getting it.
chunks.st: I received one hundred dinars from you.
chunks.stMore: Even though she has not actually received the money, the receipt serves as a means for her to waive half of the amount due to her for her marriage contract. According to Rabbi Yehuda, the financial commitment in the marriage contract is a right due to the wife, which she may waive if she chooses to do so.

chunks.en: And for a widow, one hundred,
chunks.st: And similarly, for a widow he may write one hundred dinars in the contract

chunks.en: and she writes,
chunks.st: and she may write a receipt stating:

chunks.en: I got fifty zuz from you.
chunks.st: I received from you fifty dinars.

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir says,
chunks.st: However, Rabbi Meir says: It is prohibited to do this, as

chunks.he: כָּל הַפּוֹחֵת לִבְתוּלָה מִמָּאתַיִם וּלְאַלְמָנָה מִמָּנֶה,
chunks.en: Anyone who gives a maiden less than two hundred, or a widow less than one hundred,
chunks.st: anyone who reduces the amount of the marriage contract to less than than two hundred dinars for a virgin or one hundred dinars for a widow,

chunks.en: it is not a proper marriage.
chunks.explain: It is as if there is no kesubah at all.
chunks.st: this marital relationship amounts to licentious sexual relations
chunks.stMore: because it is as if he did not write any marriage contract at all.

summary: After the erusin, a maiden gets twelve months to get ready for the wedding, and a widow thirty days. If the time came and the chasan did not marry her, he must feed her, and a Kohen may feed her terumah.

chunks.en: We give a maiden twelve months
chunks.st: gives a virgin twelve months from

chunks.en: from when the chasan asks for her, to get herself ready.
chunks.st: the time the husband asked to marry her after having betrothed her, in order to prepare herself with clothes and jewelry for the marriage.

words.en: from when he asked for her

chunks.en: And just as we give the woman time,
chunks.st: And just as one gives a woman this amount of time,

chunks.he: כָּךְ נוֹתְנִין לָאִישׁ לְפַרְנֵס אֶת עַצְמוֹ.
chunks.en: so we give the man time to get himself ready.
chunks.st: so too does one give a man an equivalent period of time to prepare himself,
chunks.stMore: as he too needs time to prepare for the marriage.

chunks.en: And a widow gets thirty days.
chunks.st: However, in the case of a widow, who already has items available from her previous marriage, she is given only thirty days to prepare.

chunks.en: If the time came and they did not get married,
chunks.st: If the appointed time for the wedding arrived and they did not get married due to some delay on the part of the husband,

chunks.en: she eats from his food, and she eats terumah.
chunks.explain: If the chasan is a Kohen.
chunks.st: then the woman may partake of his food. And if her husband is a priest, she may partake of teruma,
chunks.stMore: even if she is an Israelite woman. The tanna’im disagree about the permission granted to a priest to sustain his betrothed with teruma before she is married to him.

chunks.en: Rabbi Tarfon says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Tarfon says:

chunks.en: We may give her all of it as terumah.
chunks.st: He may give her all of her required sustenance from teruma.
chunks.stMore: During her periods of impurity, e.g., menstruation, when she cannot partake of teruma, she may sell the teruma to a priest and use the proceeds to buy non-sacred food.

chunks.en: Rabbi Akiva says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Akiva says:

chunks.en: Half regular food and half terumah.
chunks.explain: So she has food when she may not eat terumah.
chunks.st: He must give her half of her needs from non-sacred food and half may be from teruma,
chunks.stMore: so that she can eat from the non-sacred food when she is ritually impure.

summary: A yavam who is a Kohen does not let his yevamah eat terumah before the wedding. Later the beis din ruled that no kallah eats terumah until she goes under the chuppah.
stIntro: The mishna continues: A priest who is a

chunks.en: A yavam does not let her eat terumah.
chunks.st: yavam, i.e., his brother died childless after betrothing a woman, does not enable his yevama to partake of teruma by virtue of her relationship with him.

words.note: A man who must marry his brother's widow when the brother had no children.

chunks.en: If she waited six months while her chasan was alive
chunks.st: If she had completed six months of the twelve-month wait for marriage under the aegis of the husband, and then he died,

chunks.en: and six months with the yavam,
chunks.st: and she waited six more months under the aegis of the yavam;

chunks.en: or even all of it with the chasan but
chunks.st: or even if she completed all of the necessary time under the aegis of the husband except for

chunks.en: one day with the yavam,
chunks.st: one day that she was under the aegis of the yavam;

chunks.en: or all of it with the yavam but
chunks.st: or if she completed all of the necessary time under the aegis of the yavam except for

chunks.en: one day with the chasan,
chunks.st: one day that she was under the aegis of the husband,

chunks.en: she may not eat terumah.
chunks.st: she still may not partake of teruma.

chunks.en: This was the first mishnah.
chunks.st: This set of rulings, concerning the permission granted a betrothed woman whose wedding date has arrived to partake of teruma, is in accordance with the initial version of the mishna.

chunks.en: The beis din after them said,
chunks.st: However, a court that convened after them, in a later generation, said:

chunks.en: A woman may not eat terumah
chunks.st: A woman may not partake of teruma

chunks.en: until she goes under the chuppah.
chunks.st: until she has actually entered the wedding canopy.

summary: If a man makes his wife's work hekdesh, it does not work, and she keeps working and eating from it. Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yochanan HaSandlar argue about her extra earnings.

chunks.en: One who makes his wife's work hekdesh,
chunks.st: If one consecrates his wife’s earnings,
chunks.stMore: meaning anything she produces, such as thread that she spins from wool, which, according to the Sages’ ordinance, belongs to her husband,

words.note: Something given to the Beis HaMikdash.

chunks.en: she keeps working and eating from it.
chunks.st: she may work and sustain
chunks.stMore: herself from her earnings, as the consecration is ineffective.

chunks.en: About the extra, Rabbi Meir says,
chunks.st: However, there is a dispute with regard to the surplus, meaning any earnings she produces in excess of the amount she is required to produce for her husband. Rabbi Meir says:

chunks.he: הֶקְדֵּשׁ. רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הַסַּנְדְּלָר אוֹמֵר, חֻלִּין:
chunks.en: it is hekdesh. Rabbi Yochanan HaSandlar says, it is not holy.
chunks.st: The surplus is consecrated property, and Rabbi Yoḥanan the Cobbler says: The surplus is also non-sacred.

summary: A wife does certain jobs in the house, and the more maidservants she brings with her, the fewer jobs she must do. Rabbi Eliezer and Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel teach that a person should not sit doing nothing.

chunks.en: These are jobs a wife does for her husband:
chunks.st: And these are tasks that a wife must perform for her husband:

chunks.en: she grinds flour, and bakes,
chunks.st: She grinds wheat into flour, and bakes,

chunks.en: and washes clothes, cooks,
chunks.st: and washes clothes, cooks,

chunks.en: and feeds her baby,
chunks.st: and nurses her child,

chunks.en: makes his bed,
chunks.st: makes her husband’s bed,

chunks.en: and spins wool.
chunks.st: and makes thread from wool by spinning it.

chunks.en: If she brought him one maidservant,
chunks.st: If she brought him one maidservant,
chunks.stMore: i.e., brought the maidservant with her into the marriage, the maidservant will perform some of these tasks.

chunks.en: she does not grind,
chunks.st: Consequently, the wife does not need to grind,

chunks.en: and does not bake and does not wash clothes.
chunks.st: and does not need to bake, and does not need to wash clothes.

chunks.he: שְׁתַּיִם, אֵינָהּ מְבַשֶּׁלֶת וְאֵינָהּ מֵנִיקָה אֶת בְּנָהּ.
chunks.en: Two maidservants: she does not cook and does not nurse her baby.
chunks.st: If she brought him two maidservants, she does not need to cook and does not need to nurse her child
chunks.stMore: if she does not want to, but instead may give the child to a wet nurse.

chunks.en: Three: she does not make his bed
chunks.st: If she brought him three maidservants, she does not need to make his bed

chunks.en: and does not spin wool.
chunks.st: and does not need to make thread from wool.

chunks.en: Four: she sits in a fancy chair.
chunks.st: If she brought him four maidservants, she may sit in a chair [katedra]
chunks.stMore: like a queen and not do anything, as her maidservants do all of her work for her.

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Eliezer says:

chunks.en: even if she brought him a hundred maidservants,
chunks.st: Even if she brought him a hundred maidservants,

chunks.en: he makes her spin wool,
chunks.st: he can compel her to make thread from wool,

chunks.en: because doing nothing leads to bad behavior.
chunks.st: since idleness leads to licentiousness.
chunks.stMore: Consequently, it is better for a woman to be doing some kind of work.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says,
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

chunks.he: אַף הַמַּדִּיר אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ מִלַּעֲשׂוֹת מְלָאכָה,
chunks.en: Even one who makes a vow that his wife may not do any work
chunks.st: Even one who vows that his wife is prohibited from doing any work

words.en: the one who makes a vow on

chunks.en: must divorce her and give her kesubah,
chunks.st: must divorce her and give her the payment for her marriage contract,

chunks.en: because doing nothing makes a person go crazy.
chunks.st: since idleness leads to idiocy.

summary: A husband may not make a vow that keeps him away from his wife for too long. The mishnah also says how long men may travel away from home for learning or work.

chunks.en: One who makes a vow that keeps him away from his wife,
chunks.st: one who vows that his wife may not derive benefit from marital relations with him,

words.en: the one who makes a vow on

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say:

chunks.en: two weeks.
chunks.st: He may maintain this situation for up to two weeks,
chunks.stMore: but beyond that he must divorce her and give her the payment for her marriage contract.

chunks.en: Beis Hillel say,
chunks.st: Beit Hillel say:

chunks.en: one week.
chunks.st: He must divorce her if it continues beyond one week.
chunks.stMore: Apropos the husband’s obligation to his wife regarding marital relations, the Gemara mentions other aspects of this issue:

chunks.he: הַתַּלְמִידִים יוֹצְאִין לְתַלְמוּד תּוֹרָה שֶׁלֹּא בִרְשׁוּת,
chunks.en: Students may go away to learn Torah without asking
chunks.st: Students may leave their homes and travel in order to learn Torah without their wives’ permission

chunks.en: for thirty days.
chunks.st: for up to thirty days,

chunks.en: Workers, one week.
chunks.st: and laborers may leave their homes without their wives’ permission for up to one week.

chunks.en: The set times written in the Torah:
chunks.explain: How often a husband must be home with his wife.
chunks.st: The set interval defining the frequency of a husband’s conjugal obligation to his wife stated in the Torah
chunks.stMore: (see Exodus 21:10), unless the couple stipulated otherwise, varies according to the man’s occupation and proximity to his home:

chunks.en: men who do not work: every day.
chunks.st: Men of leisure, who do not work, must engage in marital relations every day,

chunks.en: Workers: twice a week.
chunks.st: laborers must do so twice a week,

chunks.en: Donkey drivers: once a week.
chunks.st: donkey drivers once a week,

chunks.en: Camel drivers: once in thirty days.
chunks.st: camel drivers once every thirty days,

chunks.en: Sailors: once in six months.
chunks.st: and sailors once every six months.

chunks.en: That is what Rabbi Eliezer says.
chunks.st: This is the statement of Rabbi Eliezer.

summary: A wife who rebels against her husband loses some of her kesubah each week, and a husband who rebels against his wife must add to it each week.

chunks.en: A wife who rebels against her husband:
chunks.st: who rebels against her husband is fined;

chunks.he: פּוֹחֲתִין לָהּ מִכְּתֻבָּתָהּ שִׁבְעָה דִינָרִין בַּשַּׁבָּת.
chunks.en: we take seven dinars a week off her kesubah.
chunks.st: her marriage contract is reduced by seven dinars each week.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: seven half-dinars.
chunks.st: Seven half-dinars [terapa’ikin] each week.

chunks.en: Until when does he keep taking off?
chunks.st: Until when does he reduce her marriage contract?

chunks.en: Until it reaches the whole kesubah.
chunks.st: Until the reductions are equivalent to her marriage contract,
chunks.stMore: i.e., until he no longer owes her any money, at which point he divorces her without any payment.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei says:

chunks.en: He keeps on taking off more,
chunks.st: He can always continue to deduct
chunks.stMore: from the sum, even beyond that which is owed to her due to her marriage contract,

chunks.he: שֶׁמָּא תִפּוֹל לָהּ יְרֻשָּׁה מִמָּקוֹם אַחֵר,
chunks.en: in case she gets an inheritance from somewhere else,
chunks.st: so that if she will receive an inheritance from another source,

chunks.en: he collects from her.
chunks.st: he can collect the extra amount from her.

chunks.en: And the same, a husband who rebels against his wife:
chunks.st: And similarly, if a man rebels against his wife, he is fined and an extra

chunks.he: מוֹסִיפִין לָהּ עַל כְּתֻבָּתָהּ שְׁלֹשָׁה דִינָרִין בַּשַּׁבָּת.
chunks.en: we add three dinars a week to her kesubah.
chunks.st: three dinars a week are added to her marriage contract.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehudah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.en: three half-dinars.
chunks.st: Three terapa’ikin.

summary: A husband who feeds his wife through someone else must give her at least a set amount of food each week. He must also give her a bed, clothing and shoes.

chunks.he: הַמַּשְׁרֶה אֶת אִשְׁתּוֹ עַל יְדֵי שָׁלִישׁ,
chunks.en: One who feeds his wife through a third person
chunks.st: feeds his wife by means of a third party
chunks.stMore: serving as a trustee, while the husband himself is not living with her for some reason,

chunks.he: לֹא יִפְחֹת לָהּ מִשְּׁנֵי קַבִּין חִטִּין,
chunks.en: must not give her less than two kav of wheat
chunks.st: he may not give her less than two kav of wheat

chunks.en: or four kav of barley.
chunks.st: or four kav of barley a week for her sustenance.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei said,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yosei said:

chunks.en: No one gave her barley except
chunks.st: Only

chunks.en: Rabbi Yishmael, who lived near Edom.
chunks.st: Rabbi Yishmael, who was near Edom, allotted her barley.

chunks.en: And he gives her half a kav
chunks.st: And he must give her half a kav of

chunks.en: of beans, and half a log of oil,
chunks.st: legumes, and half a log of oil,

chunks.en: and a kav of dried figs,
chunks.st: and a kav of dried figs

chunks.en: or a maneh of pressed figs.
chunks.st: or the weight of a maneh of fig cakes.

chunks.en: And if he does not have them,
chunks.st: And if he does not have these fruits,

chunks.en: he gives the same amount of fruit from somewhere else.
chunks.st: he must apportion for her a corresponding amount of fruit from elsewhere.

chunks.en: And he gives her a bed,
chunks.st: And he must give her a bed,

chunks.en: a soft mat, and a straw mat.
chunks.st: a soft mat, and a hard mat.

chunks.en: And he gives her a cap for her head,
chunks.st: And he must give her a cap for her head,

chunks.en: and a belt for her waist,
chunks.st: and a belt for her waist,

chunks.en: and shoes every Yom Tov,
chunks.st: and new shoes from Festival to Festival,
chunks.stMore: i.e., he must buy her new shoes each Festival.

chunks.he: וְכֵלִים שֶׁל חֲמִשִּׁים זוּז מִשָּׁנָה לְשָׁנָה.
chunks.en: and clothes worth fifty zuz every year.
chunks.st: And he must purchase garments for her with a value of fifty dinars from year to year.

chunks.en: And we do not give her
chunks.st: The mishna comments: And he may not give her

chunks.en: new clothes in the summer,
chunks.st: new clothes, which tend to be thick and warm, in the summer,

chunks.en: or worn-out clothes in the rainy season.
chunks.st: nor worn garments in the rainy season, as these are too thin and she will be cold.

chunks.en: Rather, he gives her clothes of
chunks.st: Rather, he should give her clothes at a value of

chunks.en: fifty zuz in the rainy season,
chunks.st: fifty dinars in the rainy season,

chunks.en: and she wears them when they are worn out in the summer,
chunks.st: and she covers herself with these same worn garments in the summer as well.

chunks.en: and the worn-out clothes are hers.
chunks.st: And the leftover, worn clothes belong to her.

summary: The husband also gives his wife pocket money, and she eats with him on Friday nights. In return, she spins a set amount of wool for him; a richer husband must give more.

chunks.en: He gives her a silver ma'ah for her needs,
chunks.st: he must give her another silver ma’a coin for the rest of her needs.

chunks.he: וְאוֹכֶלֶת עִמּוֹ מִלֵּילֵי שַׁבָּת לְלֵילֵי שַׁבָּת.
chunks.en: and she eats with him every Friday night.
chunks.st: And she eats with him from Shabbat evening to Shabbat evening.
chunks.stMore: Although he may provide for her sustenance via a third party throughout the week, on Shabbat evening she has the right to eat together with him.

chunks.en: And if he does not give her
chunks.st: And if he does not give her a

chunks.en: a silver ma'ah for her needs,
chunks.st: silver ma’a coin for her needs,

chunks.en: her earnings are hers.
chunks.st: her earnings belong to her.

chunks.en: And how much work does she do for him?
chunks.st: And what is the fixed amount that she must earn for him?

chunks.en: Five sela by weight of warp thread in Yehudah,
chunks.st: She must spin wool in the weight of five sela of threads of the warp in Judea,

chunks.en: which are ten sela in the Galil,
chunks.st: which are equivalent to ten sela according to the measurements of the Galilee,

chunks.he: אוֹ מִשְׁקַל עֶשֶׂר סְלָעִים עֵרֶב בִּיהוּדָה,
chunks.en: or ten sela by weight of woof thread in Yehudah,
chunks.st: or the weight of ten sela of the threads of the woof, which are easier to prepare, in Judea,

chunks.en: which are twenty sela in the Galil.
chunks.st: which are equivalent to twenty sela according to the measurements used in the Galilee.

chunks.en: And if she was nursing a baby,
chunks.st: And if she is nursing at the time,

chunks.en: we lower her work,
chunks.st: the required amount is reduced from her earnings

chunks.en: and we add to her food.
chunks.st: and is added to the sum she receives for her sustenance.

chunks.en: When is this said?
chunks.st: In what case is this statement, i.e., all these amounts and measurements, said?

chunks.en: For the poorest man in Yisrael.
chunks.st: With regard to the poorest of Jews, i.e., these are the minimum requirements.

chunks.en: But for an important man,
chunks.st: However, in the case of a financially prominent man,

chunks.en: it all goes by how important he is.
chunks.st: all the amounts are increased according to his prominence.
